title: scBaseCount: An AI agent-curated, standardized, auto-updated single-cell data repository.
journal: Cell 189(19), Sep 2026 (PMID 42753696; no PMCID). Europe PMC: isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, so no full text. Used the abstract, the GitHub READMEs (ArcInstitute/arc-virtual-cell-atlas), the bucket itself, and the bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.02.27.640494 v3 (read through a WebFetch summary only).
data_url: gs://arc-institute-virtual-cell-atlas/scbasecount/2026-01-12/ (also over HTTPS at storage.googleapis.com/arc-institute-virtual-cell-atlas/...). Contains h5ad/<5 STARsolo feature types>/<27 species>/<SRX>.h5ad, metadata/<feature>/<species>/{sample,obs}_metadata.parquet, and analysis/. The old public bucket gs://arc-scbasecount now returns 401.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Bucket access: anonymous JSON-API listing and HTTPS GET both return 200 (cache-control public). I listed all 61,378 GeneFull_Ex50pAS h5ad files: 6.44 TB total (human 35,263 files, 3.44 TB, median 70.2 MB, max 1.09 GB; mouse 2.54 TB). Sample tables: I opened sample_metadata.parquet for all 27 species in 3 feature types. GeneFull_Ex50pAS gives 61,378 SRX and 502,472,775 cells (Gene 483.2M, Velocyto 481.6M). Human: 35,263 SRX x 19 cols, 302,278,851 cells, no duplicate SRX. Columns are LLM-extracted: tissue (7,245 free-text values, 11.5% unsure/none), tissue_ontology_term_id (30% empty), disease (28% unsure/none), disease_ontology_term_id (48% null), perturbation, cell_line, tech_10x, cell_prep, single_disease_confidence (high 9,254 / medium 3,521 / low 5,613), and czi_collection_id (2,139 SRX). There is no study/SRP/GSE, sex, donor or year column. Obs tables: C. elegans obs_metadata (6.2 MB) has 325,812 rows x 10 cols and cell_type is empty for 100% of them. For the 6.0 GB human obs_metadata I read only the footer (302,278,851 rows, 289 row groups, which matches the sample sum) plus the SRX/cell_type columns of 8 row groups (2.9 MB, 7.63M cells): 69% of cells carry a cell_type, with 107 labels. h5ads: I opened 3 human files. SRX17412833 has 1,244 x 36,601 Ensembl genes, integer-valued float32 CSC counts, EM/Uniform layers, and 100% CL-labelled cells. NRX0000128 has 185 cells, all unlabelled. SRX20822906 is labelled 3_prime_gex/PBMC but has a median of 21 UMI and 1 gene per cell, yet 5,986 of its 6,891 barcodes are called 'natural killer cell'. analysis/ holds per-SRX MSigDB C8/M8 signature-score parquets (24,056 human) and embryos_labled.pq (1.88 GB, 10.2M rows; footer only). The 1,500 smallest 3'/5' GEX human SRX with at least 500 cells and a single tissue ID total 4.6 GB, but at about 0.42 KB per cell they look like near-empty libraries. A random 1,500 such SRX total 158 GB.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Per the bioRxiv v3 summary: cell types come from SE-600M embeddings plus per-tissue logistic regression trained on Tabula Sapiens. SRAgent tissue/disease accuracy is reported only qualitatively ('in most cases' vs CELLxGENE), with no per-field numbers. The State-Embedding comparison (214M scBaseCount vs 134M CELLxGENE cells): +2.24% infection, +23.9% perturbation, +10.2% AUROC / +17.2% AUPRC on DE, with 80/10/10 MLP probes on held-out datasets. The README states that disease labels are study-level and propagate to controls. The '75 tissues' definition is not given anywhere I read. I did not read the paywalled Cell methods or the SE-600M paper's evaluation tables.

a1_downloadable.note: Pass with a flag (checked). Anonymous HTTPS GET of objects returns 200 today. The documented route, however, needs a GCP project subscribed on the Marketplace (Requester Pays, free up to 2 TB/month). Arc already shut the previous public bucket (2026-03-31), so anonymous access is undocumented and could disappear.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Weak pass (checked). The SRX-level tissue/disease/perturbation/tech_10x/cell_prep columns and the cell-level cell_type column exist. None is a measured outcome. Tissue is 7,245 free-text strings, and its UBERON ID is empty or multi-term for 36% of human SRX. Disease is 28% 'unsure/none'.

a3_inputs_present.note: Pass (checked on 3 h5ads). Full UMI count matrices are included, with 36,601 Ensembl IDs plus symbols and no lookups needed. A held-out-study split, however, needs SRX-to-SRP resolution through NCBI for 35k SRX, because no study column exists.

a4_units_stated.note: Pass (checked). X holds integer-valued STARsolo UMI counts (float32), and EM/Uniform multimapper layers are named in the README. The units are implicit but standard.

a5_enough_rows.note: Pass (checked). 35,263 human SRX (61,378 across all species) and 302.3M human cells. 87 UBERON tissue IDs have at least 30 SRX, covering 18,143 SRX. The true independent unit is the study, which is uncounted.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 6.44 TB per feature type (human 3.44 TB; human obs_metadata alone 6.0 GB). A random 1,500 labelled human SRX = 158 GB to stream and pseudobulk. The only under-5 GB 1,500-SRX subset (4.6 GB) is near-empty libraries.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Fail (checked from the listing). The bucket has no precomputed pseudobulk, embedding or per-SRX feature table. Every task with at least 400 labelled units needs a bespoke 100+ GB download-and-reduce pipeline, exceeding the 50 MB-per-file rule many times over.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Pass (checked). 502,472,775 cells (GeneFull_Ex50pAS) and 27 organisms match the abstract. The human obs rows (302,278,851) equal the sample obs_count sum, and so do the C. elegans rows (325,812). Counts differ by feature type, as documented. '75 tissues' cannot be reproduced from the columns (1,784 human UBERON IDs).

a8_label_provenance.note: Fail (checked plus paper). cell_type is a model output (SE-600M + Tabula Sapiens logistic regression), applied with no QC gate: 5,986 'NK cells' were called on a 21-UMI/1-gene library. The SRX-level labels are an LLM's (SRAgent) reading of submitter text with no per-field accuracy reported, and the disease label is study-level and propagates to controls. No label traces to a physical measurement.

existing_models.name: State / SE-600M (Adduri et al., Cell 2026, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2026.07.052; bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.26.661135; HF arcinstitute/SE-600M)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract: the embeddings were trained on 167M observational cells, and perturbation discrimination improved by more than 30%. In the scBaseCount preprint, a 100M SE trained on 214M scBaseCount cells beat a CELLxGENE-trained one by +2.24% (infection), +23.9% (perturbation group) and +10.2% AUROC (DE), using 80/10/10 MLP probes on held-out datasets (WebFetch summary).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The scBaseCount authors (preprint) say cell-type annotation still needs human or community curation, cell-level donor and perturbation metadata are not recoverable from SRA, and coverage is 10x-only.

existing_models.name: scPRINT-2 (Kalfon, Peyre, Cantini; bioRxiv 10.64898/2025.12.11.693702)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract only: pre-trained on 350M cells from 16 organisms, and claims SOTA on denoising, embedding and cell-type prediction. It appeared in a Europe PMC search for 'scBaseCount', but I did not confirm that scBaseCount is in its training set.

existing_models.name: TranscriptFormer (CZI; bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.04.25.650731; pypi transcriptformer)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet only: trained on up to 112M cells from 12 species (CELLxGENE-based, not scBaseCount). On held-out species, TF-Metazoa reaches F1 0.778 for cell-type classification vs 0.701 for UCE.

existing_models.name: Bulk RNA-seq metadata prediction (Ellis et al. 2018, PMC5961118; Flynn et al. 2021, PMC8011224)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippets only: SRA-wide sex prediction accuracy is 86.3%, and about 2% of samples and 52% of studies carry a misannotated sex. Both are bulk, not single-cell.

c2_audit.note: Five searches. Cell foundation models trained on this resource are open and published by the resource's own authors, so a 'better embedding' angle is crowded. An expression-based audit of SRAgent's LLM metadata at single-cell scale is likely novel, but it is blocked by A6/A8.

backbone.name: Geneformer or scGPT (frozen) with a head on pseudobulk or cell embeddings. SE-600M is the native backbone. Not scored further.
backbone.hardware: Not assessed. The bottleneck is a 100+ GB download, not compute. SE-600M (600M params) on CPU would be slow (not timed).
backbone.licence: No data licence in the GitHub repo (the API reports none). Marketplace terms not read. SE-600M uses the Arc State Model Non-Commercial License (checked), and SRAgent is MIT.

integration.partner_dataset: CZ CELLxGENE Census, author-curated cell types for the 2,139 human SRX (53 collections, 12.5M cells) carrying czi_collection_id. GTEx bulk tissue profiles as an expression reference.
integration.join_key: czi_collection_id + cell barcode (scBaseCount) to the CELLxGENE dataset obs (the barcode format must be checked). Ensembl gene ID for GTEx. Not tested.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not scored (stopped at Part A). Candidate: how often do LLM-extracted SRA metadata and SE-600M cell-type calls disagree with author-curated CELLxGENE labels, and is disagreement explained by library quality?

controls.positive_control: Not assessed. Would be: cell_prep (single nucleus vs single cell) from the GeneFull/Gene UMI ratio (intronic fraction), and blood vs brain from pseudobulk.
controls.negative_control: Not assessed. Would be: tissue labels shuffled within study, and random features.
controls.external_validation: Not assessed. Would be: CELLxGENE author labels for the 2,139 linked SRX. There is no year or study column for a temporal or held-out-study split without NCBI lookups.

honest_claim_h3: Any model here predicts what an LLM read from SRA submitter text, or what SE-600M plus a Tabula Sapiens classifier assigned. Scope: 10x libraries that someone deposited in SRA and that survived scRecounter, including near-empty non-GEX libraries. It does not predict the true tissue, disease or cell type.
ml_idea: Unscored. Stream about 1,500 to 3,000 human SRX (about 158 GB per 1,500), reduce each to pseudobulk, and train a held-out-study classifier for tissue UBERON, cell_prep and tech_10x. Use its disagreements to audit SRAgent labels, validating on the CELLxGENE-linked subset. This is a curation-QC note rather than a biology model.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already failed. (1) Size: a random 1,500 labelled human SRX is 158 GB, and the only under-5 GB subset is near-empty libraries. (2) Provenance: SRX20822906 (3_prime_gex, PBMC) has a median of 21 UMI per cell, yet 5,986 of its barcodes are labelled 'natural killer cell'. Any rescue would first need to show that SRX-level labels agree with CELLxGENE for at least 90% of the 2,139 linked SRX.

verdict_reason: This is a 6.44 TB (human 3.44 TB) count-matrix atlas with no precomputed laptop-sized feature table (A6). Every label is either an LLM extraction from SRA text (study-level disease that leaks onto controls) or an SE-600M classifier prediction applied even to near-empty libraries (A8). The open models built on it (State SE-600M) are by the resource's own authors. Better used as a pretraining or reference source than as a labelled ML dataset.
